name: Leaderboard deltas and mobile cards

name: Japanese font toggle
summary: Global glyph font switch so kanji render the way the reader expects.

name: Incremental WaniKani caching
summary: Conditional requests and a 5-minute refresh window instead of full refetches.

name: Full-screen study modal
summary: One item at a time with WASD and arrow navigation.

name: Review and lesson modes
summary: Two distinct flows rather than one queue doing both jobs.

name: Persistent study filters
summary: Level, type and locked filters that survive a reload.

name: Local study history
summary: Self-graded attempts recorded locally, independent of WaniKani.

name: Google sign-in

name: Blind review mode
summary: Hide metadata until reveal, then grade yourself.

name: Invite-code sign-in
summary: Six-character codes for members who never use Google.
publicSummary: Invite codes for members who do not sign in with Google.

name: Admin email allowlist
summary: Admin access restricted to an explicit Google address list.

name: Bulk SRS reset
summary: Multi-select reset with staged confirmations.

summary: School-grade pills across JLPT and WaniKani explorer cards.

name: Level progress modes
summary: Item-spread drilldowns across the last five levels.

name: Study history filters
summary: SRS bucket filters and an in-modal item view.

name: News reader
summary: Paste a Japanese article URL and read it with lookup aids.

name: News kanji analysis
summary: Per-article kanji overview with WaniKani, JLPT and grade caps.

name: SRS transition feedback
summary: Show the stage an answer moved an item to.

name: Global user menu
summary: Signed-in identity card available from every page.

name: Telemetry ingest
summary: Route and client timing events collected for diagnosis.

name: Filter counts and wait sorting
summary: Every filter chip carries its own count; sort by time waiting.

name: Reading check-ins
summary: A reading calendar with ISBN book covers and incremental check-ins.

name: Reading campaigns
summary: Campaign manager, payout tuning and admin entry CRUD.

name: Reading challenge engine
summary: Challenge-scoped rewards with capped weekly bonuses.

name: Quick review mode
summary: A faster grading loop for large queues.

name: Difficulty ranking
summary: Rank reviews by measured ease so hard items surface first.

name: JLPT word examples
summary: Example vocabulary attached to each JLPT kanji.

name: Peekable meaning card
summary: Reveal a meaning without leaving the review.

name: Modal framing pass
summary: Consistent panels, background scroll locking and mobile spacing.

name: Unified glyph stats
summary: One status chip row shared by review and detail modals.

name: Server boundary hardening
summary: server-only guards so secrets cannot reach a client bundle.
publicSummary: Hardened the boundary between server and client code.

name: Deferred review writes
summary: Advance the queue immediately and persist history behind it.

name: Side-by-side reviews
summary: Compare two items during a review session.

name: Family challenge mode
summary: The first game: a shared round the family competes on.

name: Game leaderboards
summary: Competitive scoreboards with level-aware scoring.

name: Mobile status drilldown
summary: Tap a status to see its stages; filtered totals stay honest.

name: Hard mode and Ultra
summary: Harder distractors, all-item rounds and an endless Ultra run.

name: Games hub
summary: Four games behind one hub: Daily, Time Attack, Shiritori and Practice.

name: Local database and WaniKani mock
summary: Develop offline against a seeded database and a stand-in API.

name: Quad and timed scoring
summary: Four-choice rounds with per-item timing and a larger clock.

name: Read direction
summary: Answer from the reading, with named difficulty tiers.

name: Map mode
summary: The 47 prefectures, the first game that needs no WaniKani data at all.

name: Corners board and Practice lists
summary: One fixed board for every tile game; Practice drills your tagged lists.

name: Shared UI primitives
summary: ModalShell, SubjectRows and SubjectCards replace hand-rolled copies.

name: Catalog-first study queue
summary: Read subject content locally: the study page went from 15.2s to under a second warm.

name: Schema drift gate
summary: Deploys stop when the production database is behind the Prisma schema.

name: Viewer identity fix
summary: A Google viewer now resolves to an account by linked email only; the display-name fallback that granted strangers a family member's pages is gone.
publicSummary: Sign-in now matches you to your account by your linked email address.

name: Release timeline
summary: This page: every shipped and planned feature with its date, admin only.

name: Standalone JLPT study
summary: Split JLPT content from the WaniKani progress overlay so the kanji data stands on its own.

name: Display names and visibility
summary: A public Global Display Name for every member plus an opt-in visibility flag, private by default.

name: Optional WaniKani connection
summary: An account no longer requires WaniKani. The six connection fields are nullable, and every surface that used them now asks whether a connection exists instead of assuming one - WaniKani-derived boards leave unconnected accounts out rather than ranking them at level zero.

name: Capability gating
summary: One capability map decides what a member without WaniKani sees, hides or finds disabled.

name: WaniKani-free game pool
summary: Draw game rounds from the local catalogue when there is no assignment cache to draw from.

name: Connect your WaniKani account
summary: A page that explains what connecting unlocks and walks through adding the token.

name: Open Google sign-up
summary: Anyone can sign in with Google and get an account, with or without WaniKani.

name: Clans and families
summary: Members form their own group and compare inside it.

name: Global ranking opt-in
summary: A public global board that every member joins deliberately, never by default.

name: Content-based catalogue sync
summary: The sync now skips rows whose extracted content is identical, even when WaniKani bumped the timestamp for fields we never store.

name: Backfill missing catalogue subjects
summary: 64 subjects in the study queue are absent from the local catalogue and still fall through to the API.

name: Ultra as its own game kind
summary: Retire the batchSize = -1 sentinel in favour of a real enum value.

name: Shared surface primitives
summary: Move the remaining hand-rolled cards, loading states and pills onto the shared components.

name: Last play and live rounds
summary: Each hub card shows who is playing now, who played it last, and how you did.

name: JLPT old-to-N level mapping
summary: Places a pre-2010 Level 1-4 certificate on the N1-N5 scale, inferring the system from the year.

name: Viewing presence
summary: Who is looking at a game right now. Backlogged by John: not worth any performance or cost risk ahead of open signup.

name: Registration and onboarding
summary: The wizard after Google sign-in: display name, optional WaniKani token, JLPT certification, and the public-board choice.

name: JLPT level reviews
summary: Reviews that progress through an N level the way WaniKani progresses through 60. Design open.

name: Kanji coverage map
summary: Tracks which kanji WaniKani teaches, which it does not, and which it teaches that the JLPT table lacks.

name: Parallel level ladder
summary: A WaniKani-parallel progression over roughly 100 levels, covering the kanji WaniKani leaves out.

name: Compact game setup
summary: One settings row and a smaller corners picker; the duplicate exit button is gone.

name: Typecheck in the quality gate
summary: quality:check now runs tsc; it caught a fresh test bug on its first local run.

name: Feature flags
summary: Global switches toggled from an admin page, backed by a FeatureFlag table. First flag: the open-signup door, off.

name: Site version in the footer
summary: Every release bumps the version; the footer shows it and the timeline lists each release's number.

name: Release codenames
summary: Every release walks the gojuon: a two-word Japanese name per version, worn in the header like a saying.

name: Admin API namespace
summary: Every admin-gated endpoint now lives under /api/admin/; the six that were scattered across the public tree moved in.
publicSummary: Administrative endpoints were consolidated under a single namespace.

name: Honest signed-out navigation
summary: The join page sends resolved members to their own page, and the header only offers links the viewer can actually open.

name: Developer and Advanced modes
summary: Two global mode flags, toggled from the flags page; the footer wears DEV and ADV chips while they are on.

name: Timestamps and the Shelved tab
summary: Releases carry their real commit instant - John's point: a timestamp beats sort cleverness - and backlogged or killed work stays visible on its own tab.

name: Manage accounts redesign
summary: Each account row keeps one visible Open-as-user action and folds the rest into a compact overflow menu.

name: Trouble and Favourites, visible from Study
summary: The queue tag filter now shows as a chip you can clear, so a sticky Trouble filter no longer hides most of the due reviews without saying so, and the Trouble & favourites lists open from the Study page rather than only the game lobby, History and the JLPT explorer.

name: Your Lists cards match the shared card
summary: Subject cards put the level in the top-right corner the way every other surface does, and the remove button moves to the bottom-right instead of squatting where the level belongs.

name: Grouped header navigation
summary: The header drops from eleven flat items wrapping onto two rows to eight groups on one. Explore holds the three explorers, Progress holds History and Stats, Read holds Read and News, and Settings holds Libraries.

name: Release names show kana and kanji
summary: The release name prints its kana reading beside the kanji instead of hiding the kanji in a tooltip, so both scripts are readable at a glance.

name: Version number opens the release timeline
summary: For an admin the footer version number and the header motto link straight to the release timeline. Everyone else still sees them as plain text, since the page is admin-only.

name: Maps for Japan, the US and Canada
summary: Map data now covers 47 Japanese prefectures, 51 US states and 13 Canadian provinces and territories, each with capital, largest city, population, area and regional metadata, rebuilt reproducibly by the map:build scripts.

name: Study queue as a list
summary: The Study queue offers the same grid/list toggle the tagged lists and history already use, so a long queue can be scanned one line at a time. The choice is remembered per surface.

name: Geo dataset under test
summary: The map data the capital, country and size games will read is now pinned by tests: region counts, unique ids, a capital and a positive population and area for all 111 divisions, and the comparison helpers.

name: Reserved map ids for all three countries
summary: US states and Canadian provinces get their own reserved subject-id bands beside the prefectures, so map rounds for any country can ride the existing run tables. Japan keeps the exact ids recorded runs already hold.

name: One distractor rule for every map
summary: What makes a convincing wrong answer on a map - neighbours first, then region, then proximity - moves out of the Japan question builder so states and provinces use the same rule. Japan scores exactly as before.

name: School Grade explorer
summary: Kanji by Japanese school year, with the on and kun readings approved for that grade rather than every reading the character has. Covers grades 1 to 6, secondary joyo and jinmeiyo, searchable and paged.

name: Public updates page
summary: Shipped releases are public at /releases, grouped by month and expandable for the detail. Four entries that described a fixed security weakness precisely carry a cleansed public wording; the admin timeline keeps the honest text and the planned work.

name: Search across every catalogue
summary: A search box in the header and a results page that asks WaniKani, JLPT and School Grades at once, ranked into one list with exact characters and meanings first. Filter to a single catalogue with the source pills.

name: One level pill everywhere
summary: Reported by John: the level read as a pill in the lists and as faint borderless text on the study card and in the view modal. The in-glyph level and success rate are pills everywhere now.

name: Modals hold one height
summary: Reported by John: modals grew and shrank with their contents. ModalShell now owns two heights, a content one for forms and a fixed one for lists, and a test fails if a modal hand-rolls its own again.

name: Search results open where they live
summary: A search result now opens the explorer that holds it with the search already applied. Signed-out visitors keep the results as a lookup rather than being offered links that would bounce off the sign-in wall.

name: Quiz yourself on grade readings
summary: The grade grid hides its readings on request so the same page becomes a self-test: see the kanji, say the on and kun readings, select the card to check. Nothing is recorded, which is the point - it is the rehearsal, not the exam.

name: Search keeps its place on a phone
summary: The header search field cost about 150px on a phone and the mobile nav clips rather than wraps, so it had silently pushed the Admin link off the end of the row. On a phone it is now the icon alone, linking to the search page.

name: Stop showing compound-only readings
summary: Reported by John: the grade cards listed readings a character never has on its own. KANJIDIC hyphenates compound-only forms, and 31 of the 80 first-grade entries carried one, so the King card claimed a kun reading of -nou that only exists inside a compound. Those are filtered out of the display.

name: Animated stroke order
summary: Every kanji can be watched being written, one stroke at a time, with optional stroke numbers. Stroke data comes from KanjiVG under CC BY-SA, credited on every animation, and is rebuilt reproducibly from a pinned commit with pnpm strokes:build. Covers all 2,899 school-grade characters.

name: Compare the printed kanji with the strokes
summary: The stroke-order view shows the printed character beside the animation, so a child copying strokes has the real shape to compare against, with the grade, JLPT and WaniKani levels, frequency rank and readings underneath.

name: Official readings from the joyo table
summary: Reported by John: the grade cards listed every reading a character has ever taken. They now use the readings from the joyo table, which is the cabinet-notified list for general use - so King correctly shows no kun reading, Sound files its in reading as on, and Life drops from twenty-one readings to ten. Both fonts are shown in the stroke view for comparison.

name: Stroke order beyond the grades page
summary: Stroke order moves into a shared button any surface can drop in, and the glyph viewer gains it for kanji. The data now covers every WaniKani kanji as well as the school grades - the characters WaniKani teaches past the joyo list were silently missing, and those are the ones a learner is least sure how to write.

name: Refresh the catalogue export
summary: The script that exports the WaniKani catalogue could not run at all - it imported a server-only module - so its committed snapshot had drifted to 3,930 of 9,324 subjects. Fixed and regenerated, and dropping the raw payload makes the complete export smaller than the stale one was.

name: Official readings on every surface
summary: The grade explorer was not the only place showing readings a character never takes on its own: 245 of the 2,211 JLPT kanji carried them too, so the JLPT explorer, the glyph viewer and search all did. One shared helper now prefers the joyo table wherever readings leave the database.

name: Say what the readings actually are
summary: The grade page claimed its readings were the ones approved for that school year. They are the joyo table's, which is the official list for general use and is not split by year, so the copy now says so.

name: Stroke order from search
summary: A kanji in the search results opens its stroke order without leaving the page. Radicals and vocabulary do not offer it, since neither is a single character with a stroke sequence.

name: Printable writing practice
summary: A printable tracing sheet for any school grade: each character once at full weight to copy, faint repeats to trace, then empty squares to write unaided, with the guide lines a Japanese workbook uses. Drawn from the real stroke paths rather than a greyed-out font.

name: Practice sheets for any list
summary: Writing practice is no longer only for school grades: the same sheet prints a WaniKani level or a JLPT level, so the ladder you are actually climbing is the one you can practise writing.

name: Practice reachable from the nav
summary: Writing practice joins the Explore group instead of hiding behind the grades page, and the sheet keeps the site header on screen while dropping it for print. A nested page no longer lights up its parent's tab as well as its own.

name: An account has its own address
summary: Every account gets a permanent slug and a display name it can change. Pages resolve by either the slug or the old WaniKani username, so links already shared keep working, and an account with no WaniKani connection is now reachable at all.

name: The study queue menu fits on a phone again
summary: The Reviews menu was anchored to its right edge to keep it on screen on a desktop, which pushed it off the left edge on a phone, where the panel is nearly as wide as the display. It now anchors left on small screens and flips right only where there is room.

name: Layout checks at phone, tablet and desktop
summary: Every page is now loaded at three widths and checked for anything hanging outside the screen, with the study menus opened and checked the same way. Its first run found the library upload card running off the side of a phone, which is now fixed.

name: A profile page for every member
summary: Settings now opens on a profile: change the name other members see, record a JLPT certificate, and read a table of every game you have finished. WaniKani level stays read-only because WaniKani sets it, and an account with no WaniKani connection reads Not connected instead of showing a blank.

name: Members without WaniKani can reach their own pages
summary: Page access matched on a WaniKani username, so an account that signed in with Google and never connected WaniKani was turned away from every page it owns - its own profile included - while its API calls kept working. Access now matches the permanent slug first and falls back to the username, so links shared earlier still resolve.

name: The sign-in screen stops offering a door that goes nowhere
summary: Back to leaderboard is hidden for viewers the home page would send straight back, so the button no longer returns you to the page you are already reading. The screen also sends a member who has an account but no WaniKani connection to their own page instead of bouncing them through the invite form.

name: Signing in and out follows one path
summary: Asking for the login page while already signed in answered with a sign-out screen. It now takes you where you were headed, or to your own page. The sign-out tab links straight to the one screen that signs you out instead of bouncing through a redirect with no page of its own, and calls it Sign out, the wording used everywhere else.

name: Signing up, and choosing who can see you
summary: A newcomer now gets a welcome instead of a locked door: what UmaKuma is, that WaniKani is not required, a name, and a choice of who can see them, which they can change on their profile whenever they like. Leaderboards respect that choice. Who may join, what they start on and which questions are asked are all set from a new admin page, and it ships closed.

name: One menu that knows what the header knows
summary: The account menu kept its own copy of the navigation beside the header's, and the two had drifted apart. It now reads the same sections the header does, so nothing can go missing again. On a desktop it drops the navigation entirely, since the header already shows it, and keeps only your account, settings, admin and preferences. Settings moves out of the header into the menu, and Updates is reachable without hunting for the version number in the footer.

name: Rows for the grade explorer, and quieter cards
summary: The grade explorer can be read as rows as well as cards, which is how you scan a whole school year and the only way to see a kanji with ten kun readings in full. The stroke control no longer sits on every card: it appears when you hover, or always where there is no hover to give, which also fixes it covering the end of a long reading.

name: Existing members stay on the public leaderboard
summary: Accounts that predate the visibility setting now read as public, which is what they already were. Reading them as members-only had emptied the leaderboard for anyone who was not signed in. New accounts still start private, where no audience is being taken away.

name: The welcome page accepts an invite session
summary: An invited member may have no Google account at all, and the welcome page assumed one - sending them to the sign-in screen from a page they were entitled to open. It now accepts either kind of session and routes them to their own page.

name: Any kanji, in detail, at its own address
summary: The stroke-order panel is now a shared component any surface can open, and every kanji has a public page you can send to someone. Selecting a card in the grade explorer opens it, which is how every other subject grid already behaved. The header carries the readings as well as the meaning, since a reader knows 何 by なに before they know it by what, with the stroke count beside it and the credit centred at the foot.

name: Updates leads with the release name
summary: Each release now shows its codename on the row rather than only inside it, since that is the part anyone remembers. Months collapse, and an admin reaches the release admin page from here instead of finding their own way.

name: A stroke-order sheet, and honesty about phones
summary: Writing practice can now be printed as a stroke-order chart: one numbered square per stroke, the character built up to that point with the newest stroke picked out. A character of more than eight strokes runs onto a second row instead of shrinking the squares. On a phone the sheet now says plainly that it wants a bigger screen, rather than rendering squares too small to write inside.

name: The practice sheet keeps the sheet you chose
summary: Changing grade or turning the page dropped you back to the tracing sheet, because only the sheet toggle carried the choice. Every link on the page keeps it now.

name: The stroke sheet reads like a practice book
summary: Every row is a full eight squares now: the finished character faintly at the start to work from, the strokes after it, and empty squares filling out the rest of the line. Each row is also titled with the character itself before its meaning.

name: Change the sheet without leaving it
summary: Selecting the source you are already on opens a second row holding every value it offers: the eight school grades, sixty WaniKani levels or five JLPT levels. Changing sheet meant going back to the grade page and in again, which made a page you might print several of from harder to use than it needed to be.

name: Rows on every explorer, and headers that line up
summary: The WaniKani and JLPT explorers can be read as rows as well as cards, which the grade explorer already offered and they did not. The four pages behind the Explore tabs also shared no wrapper, so the sub-nav sat at three different heights and moving between tabs nudged the whole header; they now agree exactly.

name: The practice sheet asks instead of assuming
summary: Whether the finished character sits in the first column is now a checkbox rather than a decision made for you, and the readings can print beside each meaning. The chooser also closes when you pick what is already picked, or with a Done button at the end of the row.

name: Print a sheet from your own lists
summary: Trouble and Favourites are now sources for a writing sheet, offered from the practice page itself rather than only where the tags were made. They stay quiet until the control row is hovered, and appear always on a touch screen where there is no hover to give.

name: Grades reads like its sibling explorers
summary: Filters and results shared one card on the grade explorer, divided by a hairline, while both other explorers keep them in separate cards. They are separate here too now, and the result count sits with the results rather than with the filters.

name: Turning off the finished character clears its square
summary: The option reached the stroke-order sheet but not the tracing sheet, which kept printing the character solid in the first square - the one thing the option exists to remove. It is now an empty square to write in, like the rest of the row.

name: The JLPT as it was before 2010
summary: The explorer and the writing sheet both offer the four levels the test ran until 2009, for anyone who sat it then. Both schemes count down, so old Level 4 is the beginner paper and matches N5 rather than N4 - and N3 is absent, because it was added in 2010 to bridge old Levels 3 and 2. The explorer says so rather than inventing a mapping.

name: Map mode reaches the United States and Canada
summary: Fifty-one states and thirteen provinces and territories join the forty-seven prefectures, as a bonus over the same board rather than a second game. Japan stays the default everywhere, and nothing new is stored: each question's target already carries its country in its id range, so runs recorded before this still read as Japan.

name: Choose the country you play the map on
summary: Map mode's setup now offers Japan, the United States or Canada, and the item count follows the choice - forty-seven, fifty-one or thirteen. Only Map shows the control, because only Map plays somewhere. Adding Europe or Asia later is a dataset and a line in one list, not a new game.

name: The map board follows the question
summary: A Canadian round drew the Japanese coastline: the question knew its country and the board did not. The board now reads the country off the question, and the lobby offers only countries whose maps are real - the American and Canadian outlines are placeholder shapes, so they wait until that is fixed rather than being offered unplayable.

name: Real maps for the United States and Canada
summary: Map mode plays on all three countries. The American and Canadian outlines were hand-drawn placeholders - Ontario was five points - and are now built from the Census Bureau and Natural Earth by scripts that can be re-run when a boundary changes. Neighbours come from the map itself, so the wrong answers are the places next door.

name: Counts where you choose, preferences where your account is
summary: The writing sheet's second row of chips now carries counts, so picking a grade or level is no longer a choice between bare numbers. Theme and Japanese font move from the account menu onto the profile, which already held the name and the visibility - one home for how you want UmaKuma to be rather than two.

name: Every choice visible, and one rule for page width
summary: Two small regions close together put their handles in the same few pixels, so a choice could be hidden behind another and never clicked - Prince Edward Island behind Nova Scotia. A handle now hangs below its region when the space above is taken. Scoreboards say which country a map run was played on, and member pages follow one width rule instead of three.

name: Name the capital, find the region
summary: Map mode can ask by capital city: the prompt names the seat of government and the answer is the region that governs from it. Bismarck is North Dakota, Victoria is British Columbia. It works on all three countries, because every dataset already recorded a capital for every region.

name: Capitals that actually ask something
summary: The capitals round now skips the twenty-nine Japanese prefectures that share their capital's name, so it asks the eighteen worth knowing: 札幌市 is Hokkaido, 横浜市 is Kanagawa, 名古屋市 is Aichi. Japanese capitals are written in kanji now too, matching the tiles rather than sitting in romaji in a Japanese round.

name: Pagers where the page needs them
summary: Paging is a shared component now, and where it sits is the surface's choice: top, bottom, both or none. The writing practice sheet takes both, because its only Next link used to be three thousand pixels below the fold, past three sheets of empty tracing squares.

name: A sheet that prints like a worksheet
summary: Printing a writing sheet now gives you a worksheet: Letter with proper margins, a Name and Date rule at the top, characters that never split across a page break, and none of the site's footer or version banner. The faint tracing characters print faintly instead of vanishing into the browser's ink saving.

name: Squares sized for who is writing
summary: The writing sheet offers three square sizes. Large gives a child six big boxes to form characters in; Small gives an adult ten smaller ones and an extra tracing repetition, which is what copying at volume actually wants. Medium is the practice-book square the sheet always had.

name: Prints on the paper you have
summary: The sheet named Letter as its paper size, which overrode the printer: an A4 tray produced a Letter page scaled down inside it. It now pins only the orientation and lets the paper be whatever is loaded, so A4 and 8.5x11 both come out filling the page.
